result.reason: The file conforms to the Service Conventions specification. It exports a single entry point, `run(store, input)`, taking the Store first and a single input object, returning `Result<number>` from the domain types. The module name `apply-discount.ts` is verb-first kebab-case. All domain failures are returned as `{ ok: false, error }` values with no exceptions, and each error message names what was wrong and what would be accepted instead (e.g., listing valid parlors or active codes). Validation reads top-to-bottom before the happy path, the service does one thing, and there is no I/O beyond the injected Store (the `ACTIVE_CODES` constant is inert data, not I/O). The doc comment states the purpose in one sentence and enumerates all three domain failure modes, matching the actual error paths.

The service module satisfies all criteria defined in the specification: it exports exactly one entry point function named 'run' that takes Store first and a single input object, returns a Result<T>; follows domain failures as values with consumer-friendly error messages; validates input before any work; does one thing (applies discount codes); has no I/O except through injected Store; and includes comprehensive documentation with purpose and failure modes.
